preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 5000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(n == int(n) and m == int(m) and 2 <= n <= 100 and 2 <= m <= 100 for n, m in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::] if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit()))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line contains two integers n and m (2 ≤ n, m ≤ 100) representing the dimensions of the binary table.

preconditions.expression: all(len(row) == m and all(c in '01' for c in row) for row in (stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1)))
preconditions.description: Each test case is followed by n lines of binary strings of length m, where each character is either '0' or '1'.

preconditions.expression: sum(n * m for n, m in (line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::] if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit())) <= 20000
preconditions.description: The sum of n*m for all test cases does not exceed 20000.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.splitlines()) == 1 + k for k in (int(stdout.splitlines()[i]) for i in range(0, len(stdout.splitlines()), 1 + int(stdout.splitlines()[i]))))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output starts with an integer k (0 ≤ k ≤ n*m) representing the number of operations.
Each operation is described by six integers x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3 (1 ≤ x1, x2, x3 ≤ n, 1 ≤ y1, y2, y3 ≤ m) representing the coordinates of three distinct cells in a 2×2 square.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= n and 1 <= int(y) <= m for x, y in (line.split()[::2], line.split()[1::2]) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: All coordinates in the operations are within the bounds of the table (1 ≤ x ≤ n, 1 ≤ y ≤ m).

postconditions.expression: all(any((abs(int(x1) - int(x2)) <= 1 and abs(int(y1) - int(y2)) <= 1) for x1, y1, x2, y2 in [(line.split()[0], line.split()[1]), (line.split()[0], line.split()[3]), (line.split()[0], line.split()[5]), (line.split()[2], line.split()[3]), (line.split()[2], line.split()[5]), (line.split()[4], line.split()[5])]) for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The three cells in each operation must belong to some 2×2 square (i.e., all pairs of cells must be within a 2×2 grid).

postconditions.expression: all(len(set((int(x1), int(y1)), (int(x2), int(y2)), (int(x3), int(y3)))) == 3 for x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3 in (line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: The three cells in each operation must be distinct.

postconditions.expression: all(any((int(x1) == int(x2) and int(x2) == int(x3) and abs(int(y1) - int(y2)) <= 1 and abs(int(y2) - int(y3)) <= 1) or (int(y1) == int(y2) and int(y2) == int(y3) and abs(int(x1) - int(x2)) <= 1 and abs(int(x2) - int(x3)) <= 1) for x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3 in (line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]))
postconditions.description: The three cells in each operation must be either in the same row or the same column within a 2×2 square.

postconditions.expression: all(all(row == '0' * m for row in (stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1))) if k == 0 else True)
postconditions.description: If k = 0, the table must already be all zeros (no operations needed).

postconditions.expression: all(all(all(row[j] == '0' for j in range(m)) for row in (stdin.splitlines()[i:i+n] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), n+1))) if k > 0 else True)
postconditions.description: If k > 0, the sequence of operations must transform the table to all zeros.
